# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.

## G6 Cross-GDD edits are now allowed
A blocker that needs a sibling GDD to change is fixed IN the sibling. Owner wins (G1): the registry `source:` GDD, else the publisher of the field/signal, keeps its value; the other conforms. Each file has exactly one writer per pass; requests to another file go to that file's writer.
Classify every blocker first: **CONFLICT** (the same thing has two values/contracts in two GDDs) -> the owner's value stands and the other GDD conforms; **GAP** (the owner lacks a surface, exemption, field or signal that a consumer's user-ruled or delegated-ruled behaviour requires, e.g. Interaction's act_gate exempt list lacking self-patch, HUD lacking a give_up surface) -> the OWNER ADDS it, and the consumer's requirement is the spec. Never "fix" a gap by removing the consumer's ruled behaviour.
Precedence: where R1 text conflicts with R13/R14, R13/R14 win; re-mark such text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14".

## R12 Reference machines and build (closes X14; supersedes R11)
- **RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop):** Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms.
- **RM-DECK (handheld):** Steam Deck LCD (2022), SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 33.3 ms.
- **Build type for every wall-clock figure:** a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus` (project.godot), vsync on, the pipeline's warm-up of 120 frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result.
- **P99 headroom:** pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck).
- The developer's machine is not a reference machine; figures from it are indicative only.
- Recorded in `project.yaml` as `qa.min_spec` (done by the orchestrator). In GDDs: replace "X14 open / not named / [blocked: reference hardware]" with the named machines; performance ACs become gated on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK at the spike (still measured at the spike, so a value not yet measured is "pending spike", not "blocked").

## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

With the avatar still the lag is zero and a still mouse gives a constant aim whatever the look-ahead does; **when a run starts or stops the lag grows or shrinks (≤ 32.4 px at `v_run`, up to ≈ 21.6 px at walk) and a still mouse turns the beam by the geometry of that lag** (about 28° for a cursor 60 px from the avatar at full lag, 9° at 200 px), with no input from the player. This is accepted because the reference the hidden cursor is read against is the *picture* (the camera's follow pose), which is also what the player sees move; the review's alternative of anchoring on the avatar position would hold the beam rigid against the hand but put the hidden-cursor reference up to 104 px (32.4 px of lag plus the 72 px look-ahead) off the drawn avatar. Neither form puts the reference on the drawn avatar; the cost of the chosen form is bounded and is measured by the target-acquisition item of the motion-integrity spike (Game Feel, "Target acquisition protocol"), with pre-recorded fallbacks. Pillar 1's "the beam is your hand" is protected where it matters most: the beam never moves when the avatar is still, and its origin and shape are untouched. The beam is **drawn** from the real `CHEST_POINT` (PC-5 below); only the *measurement* uses the fixed reference, so a facing flip (the chest point moves up to 4 px horizontally, more vertically across rows) can never move the aim, and the sheet/flip/beam limit cycle with a near cursor cannot occur. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: loop break and facing-independent aim origin; the 2026-10-26 us

content.content:
**D.8 Facing from committed aim — sector hysteresis and overrides**

The `facing` formula (registry: `facing_from_aim`; `controller.step`, every tick, no easing; rules evaluated top-down, first match wins) is defined as:

`facing = facing_prev if loco_state ∈ {STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD} (rule 1, frozen);  channel_face if loco_state == CHANNELLING (rule 2, the stored octant written by `set_channel_ref` at channel start; the chest lamp still follows aim);  octant if loco_state == RUN (rule 3);  f_aim if aim_live (rule 4);  octant if octant ≠ NONE (rule 5);  facing_prev otherwise (rule 6)`

Derived: `f_aim_raw = posmod(floor((aim_angle + 256) / 512), 8)` (`posmod`, as every `mod` in D.7 and D.8)
Derived: `f_aim = f_aim_raw if cdist(aim_angle, 512 × facing_prev) > 256 + FACING_HYSTERESIS, else facing_prev`
Derived: `sheet = facing ∈ {3, 4, 5} ? mirror_of(facing) : facing; flip_h = facing ∈ {3, 4, 5}` (NW→NE, W→E, SW→SE)

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| aim_angle | int | 0–4095 | calculated (`controller.state`, last applied `set_aim`) | Committed aim |
| facing_prev | int | 0–7 | calculated (`controller.state.facing` last tick; spawn **6 = S**) | Previous facing |
| FACING_HYSTERESIS | int | 32–96 (**64** = 1/64 turn = 5.625°) | data file | Extra distance past a sector boundary (256 units = 22.5°) before facing flips; must be ≥ `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` (one send can never straddle it) and < 256 |
| aim_live | bool | — | calculated (`controller.state.aim_live`, carried on `set_aim` — D.7) | Mouse: always true; stick: deflected past `AIM_DEADZONE`; keys: an aim key held; `FOLLOW_ALWAYS`: never |
| octant | int | 0–8 | calculated | Movement octant |
| channel_face | int | 0–7 or none | stored (`controller.state.channel_face`, written by `set_channel_ref`'s `face_octant` = `octant_of(target anchor − foot)` computed by the channel owner at the `begin_*` apply; cleared with `channel_ref`) | The locked work-facing octant; stored data, so a MIRROR client reads it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
| facing | int | 0–7 | calculated | Published facing |
| flip_h | bool | — | calculated (Presenter) | Mirror flag for the three mirrored facings |

**Output Range:** Eight values, every tick, from committed state only. The hysteresis band is 2 × 64 = 128 units = 11.25° wide centred on each boundary; a mouse resting on a boundary never flickers. Facing flips in a single tick (a 180° flick is one tick, D.7's send permitting). The overrides are evaluated top-down and the first match wins, so a runner's facing ignores aim entirely and a stagger freezes whatever was there. `aim_live` must travel with `set_aim` as a boolean payload field *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; PC-4 rules 4–6 branch on it, so it is sim state, and the Adapter is the only thing that knows whether a stick is deflected)*. Co-op: `facing` itself is in `controller.state` and replicates; a MIRROR client never recomputes it from aim, which is why the replicated aim's coarsening bound (≤ `FACING_HYSTERESIS`) is about the *beam* agreeing with the facing, not the facing itself.
**Example:** `aim_angle = 764` (67.17°): `f_aim_raw = floor(1020 / 512) = 1 (NE)`; centre of NE is 512, `cdist(764, 512) = 252 ≤ 320` → if `facing_prev = NE` hold NE; if `facing_prev = E (0)`, `cdist(764, 0) = 764 > 320` → NE. Lower half-plane: `aim_angle = 3332` (SE of the avatar, −67.17°) → `f_aim_raw = posmod(floor(3588 / 512), 8) = 7 (SE)`; `aim_angle = 4095` → `floor(4351 / 512) = 8 → posmod 0 (E)`; due south `3072` → `floor(3328 / 512) = 6 (S)`. `aim_angle` is already `posmod`-wrapped by D.7, so `f_aim_raw` is never negative; `cdist` uses `posmod` too *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: 765 → 764 and the wrap examples)*. Mouse drifts to `aim_angle = 800` (70.3°): `cdist(800, 512) = 288 ≤ 320` → NE holds (raw would say N from 768). At 833 (73.2°): `289 → 321 > 320` → N. Running SW while aiming NE → `facing = 5 (SW)`, `sheet = SE`, `flip_h = true`; the beam light still rotates to 67° from the mirrored chest point.

**D.9 Reach test and focus score**

The `in_reach` formula (sim-side, Interaction's `validate`; integer-only) is defined as:

`in_reach(o) = d² ≤ REACH_PX²  ∧  D > 0  ∧  D² × 1000 ≥ COS2_REACH × 65536 × d²  ∧  lit(o)`

Derived: `r = anchor_o − foot; d² = r.x² + r.y²; D = dot(UNIT[facing], r)` (integer, 1/256 scale); `COS2_REACH = round(1000 × cos²(REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG)) = 117`
Derived (Adapter-side, per render frame, float permitted — it chooses a target, the sim re-checks it): `score(o) = d / REACH_PX + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × θ_a / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` over candidates with `in_reach(o)`
Derived: `focus = argmin score`, kept on the current focus unless `score(best) < score(current) − FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` or the current focus is no longer a candidate; ties → smaller `θ_a`, then smaller entity id

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| anchor_o | vec2 int | — | calculated (Interaction's per-object interaction anchor; default = footprint centre) | Where the object is "at" for reach |
| foot | vec2 int | — | calculated (`body.state.pos_curr`, aliased `pos`; horizontally centred, the foot box's top row) | Foot origin *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)* |
| d | float / d² int | 0–REACH_PX | calculated | Distance to the anchor; the sim compares squares |
| REACH_PX | int | 48–96 (**72**) base px | data file | Reach radius — 1.5 tiles; includes the diagonal neighbour at 48√2 = 67.9 |
| UNIT[facing] | vec2 int | D.3 table | constant | Facing direction at 1/256 scale (angle `θ_f` is measured from it); the diagonal entries are 255.97/256 of unit length — a 0.02 % bias on the arc edge, accepted |
| D | int | — | calculated | `dot(UNIT[facing], r)`; all terms of `in_reach` are integers (64-bit: `D²` ≤ (256 × 96 × 2)² ≈ 2.4 × 10^9, × 1000 fits) |
| REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG | float | 45–90 (**70**) | data file | Half-angle of the reach sector about **facing** |
| θ_f | float | 0–180° | calculated | Angle between facing and `r` — the arc test |
| θ_a | float | 0–180° | calculated (Adapter) | Angle between the **ground-projected aim** and `r` — the score weight. Mouse: the direction from `foot` to `cursor_aim_world` (D.7), so pointing the lamp straight at a floor object scores θ_a ≈ 0 instead of the 30° the chest-height origin would give; stick and keys: the committed `aim_angle` (a direction only). Presentation-side only; `in_reach` and the sim never see it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| lit(o) | bool | — | calculated (Emitter State's exposure query ≥ the technical-artist's threshold) | Object is lit |
| FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT | float | 0.5–2.0 (**1.0**) | data file | Weight of aim against proximity |
| FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN | float | 0–0.25 (**0.10**) | data file | Score advantage a challenger needs to take focus *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; two near-equal candidates would otherwise trade the prompt every frame as the aim jitters within one quantum)* |
| in_reach | bool | — | calculated | Candidate predicate; also the sim's validation of the Adapter's chosen target |
| score | float | 0–≈ 2.4 at defaults | calculated | Lower is better |

content.content:
**D.13 Noise stimulus — per tick, per tile, per second**

The `noise_tick` formula (hook `controller.noise`, divisor 1, `after: [body.integrate]` — a second Controller hook, because `controller.step` runs before Body and cannot see this tick's motion (Ship Body CP-3, option b); on each tick with `noise_T > 0` it calls `push_stimulus(NOISE, actor, class)` with `class` = WALK, RUN or CARRY from `loco_state`, and Attention's intake maps the class to its magnitude) is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics, attention-system)*

`noise_T = (moved_x, moved_y) ≠ (0, 0) ? NOISE[loco_state] : 0`, where `NOISE` is **total** over `loco_state`: `NOISE[WALK] = 1`, `NOISE[RUN] = 4`, `NOISE[CARRY_WALK] = 1`, and 0 for every other state (`IDLE`, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD`, `IN_POD`), so displacement that is not locomotion (a pod hop's body transfer, a shove) pushes no gait stimulus *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; with `(moved_x, moved_y) = moved(actor) := pos_curr − pos_prev` (Body's derived read, valid only from a hook after `body.integrate`)

Derived: `noise_per_tile = NOISE[g] × TILE_PX / v_g`
Derived: `noise_per_s = NOISE[g] × TICK_RATE`
Derived: `ratio_tile(run : walk) = (NOISE_RUN / NOISE_WALK) × (v_walk / v_run)`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| NOISE[g] (registry: `NOISE_PER_TICK`) | int | ratio-preserving (**WALK 1, RUN 4, CARRY_WALK 1**; 0 for every non-locomotion state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) | data file (Attention units, 1 AU = one walking tick; this GDD owns the gait table and Attention's intake maps each `push_stimulus` class to it; the 4 : 1 ratio is the design) | Stimulus per moving tick by locomotion state (RUN includes its ramp ticks: the lean is already playing) |
| moved_x, moved_y | int | — | calculated (D.3; Body's derived `moved(actor)`, read in `controller.noise`) | Post-collision motion; a body pushing a wall makes no footsteps |
| v_g | int | 1–3 | data file | Gait speed |
| noise_T | int | {0, 1, 4} | calculated | Derived magnitude of this tick's push (the push itself carries the class WALK / RUN / CARRY) |
| noise_per_tile | int | 24 / 64 / 48 | calculated | Walk / run / carry |
| noise_per_s | int | 60 / 240 / 60 | calculated | Walk / run / carry while moving |
| ratio_tile | float | 2.67 | calculated | Running's per-tile cost relative to walking |

**Output Range:** Per tick 0, 1 or 4; Attention (divisor 6) sees the sum of up to six ticks, 0–24 per run. Running is 4× louder per second and **2.67× louder per tile** (`4 × 2/3`) — the Section G invariant `ratio_tile > 1` is what makes running a real trade rather than a free retreat; it would fail if `NOISE_RUN / NOISE_WALK ≤ v_run / v_walk = 1.5`. Carrying is as loud per second as walking but **2× louder per tile** (48 vs 24) because it is slower — an intended consequence (extraction under rising Attention is the sortie's tension), recorded here so a balance pass does not read it as an error. Noise is a function of locomotion state and motion only; nothing in it reads Attention, rhythm or sanity.
**Example:** A 10-tile corridor: walked in 240 ticks → 240 noise; run in 160 ticks (+ 6 ramp ticks at 4) → ≈ 640 noise; carried in 480 ticks → 480 noise. Walking into a wall for 60 ticks → 0.

185 **PC-10. The two rhythms in the controller.** Nothing in this system changes between boarding, the Tell and breach: no adrenaline, no speed buff, no reduced noise, no "panic" input changes. **The breach is frantic because of what moves, not because the body changes** (art bible 2.8). Running is allowed everywhere and is **noisy**: the hook `controller.noise` (divisor 1, `after: [body.integrate]`, D.13) calls Attention's `push_stimulus(NOISE, actor, class)` once on each tick the actor moved, with `class` = WALK, RUN or CARRY from `loco_state`; the class magnitudes are this GDD's gait table `NOISE_WALK` = 1, `NOISE_RUN` = 4, `NOISE_CARRY` = 1 (registry: `NOISE_PER_TICK`; Attention units, 1 AU = one walking tick). Running is 1.5× faster and 4× louder per tick, ≈ 2.7× louder per tile: running never dominates walking for stealth and is a real trade in a retreat. The player's **own running footsteps are audible and distinct from walking** — the only "meter" for noise (audio-director; captions name "your running" for the accessibility-specialist). Tool noise is pushed by Interaction (classes TOOL / LOUD); Suit pushes none at MVP; beam exposure is Emitter State's. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from attention-system, ship-body-and-interior-physics)*

65 *Contexts.* Exactly one context is active: `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`. Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch; entering `chart_table` or `chat` also submits `cancel_channel` for a hold- **or** toggle-mode channel (in the co-op overlay the sim keeps running and a channel the player cannot see must not keep burning); entering `inspect_card` does **not** cancel the channel, so the Pillar 4 "second instrument" check on the pipe being welded is free (the zeroed move intent is not a move, the channel continues, `interact` is still tracked for hold mode and a release inside the card still cancels; `cancel` closes the card first and a second `cancel` cancels the channel). **Movement closes the card** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D94, the Controller's context-matrix amendment adopted; the In-World Instruments fallback "buffer and replay the first move press" is void)*: a **fresh** movement input in `inspect_card` (a `move_*` key going down, or the left stick crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`) returns the context to `gameplay` **and** submits `set_move_intent` for that octant in the same frame, in that order, so the first press both closes the card and moves the avatar (nothing is swallowed, nothing is buffered). A direction already held when the card opened is latched and does not count until it is released (or the stick falls below the exit band) and pressed again, so opening the card while walking does not close it on the next frame. A move that closes the card while a channel is running is an ordinary non-`NONE` move intent and aborts the channel exactly as it does in `gameplay`. Any transition of `loco_state` to `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD` returns the context to `gameplay` on the same frame (the Adapter observes the published state; the card or overlay closes and the cursor is hidden again). Pause is reachable in every state including `DOWNED`: `chart_table` and `request_pause` are Adapter-level and never gated by `loco_state`. The full **context × action matrix** is in the table below. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; supersedes the earlier "cancel all channels on every non-`gameplay` entry" note for `inspect_card` only. Routed to Instruments and Interaction as a cross-GDD note.)* The OS cursor is **hidden and confined** in `gameplay` (HUD HS-52: no cursor in `gameplay`; the beam is the pointer) and **shown and released** in `chart_table` and `chat`; in `inspect_card` it stays **hidden and inert** (HUD HS-52: `set_aim` stays live there, and a visible cursor would be a second pointer over the beam; PC-16). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from hud-and-suit-layer, in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view; cursor visibility in `inspect_card` corrected 2026-10-27 — design review, HS-52 owns it)* Zoom is reachable from `gameplay` and `inspect_card`, and pause from `gameplay` (from `inspect_card` the firs
=====
169 *Cursor warp and source handover (one Adapter rule, presentation-local).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the 35 px origin offset does not scale with `k`, so a zoom step turned the beam under a still mouse, and the first mouse movement after stick use snapped the beam to a stale cursor position; the earlier acceptance criteria allowed both.)* The OS cursor is hidden and confined in `gameplay`, so the Adapter may reposition it without the player seeing a pointer move. **(i) Zoom edge:** on a `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` step (the pipeline's `RESCALING` frame) the Adapter warps the hidden cursor to `picture_centre + cursor_off_old × k_eff_new`, keeping `cursor_off` (base px) and therefore `aim_q` unchanged within ±1 unit; if the target position falls outside the window the warp clamps and the aim may differ (the confinement rectangle is the window, Edge Cases). **(ii) Handover to the mouse:** while the aim source is STICK or KEYS the mouse takes over only after `AIM_MOUSE_TAKEOVER_PX` (default 6 physical window px, **[PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike]**, range 2–16) of accumulated cursor travel, so a nudged desk does not hijack the lamp; at takeover the Adapter first warps the cursor to the point whose direction from `AIM_ORIGIN` is the current raw aim and whose radius is `max(last |r|, AIM_WARP_RADIUS_PX)` (default 48 base px, **[PLACEHOLDER]**, range 16–96), so the first mouse sample holds the aim it found instead of jumping to a stale position. **(iii) `aim_source` ∈ {AUTO, MOUSE, STICK, KEYS}:** `AUTO` (default) follows the last aim axis, with (ii) applied on a handover to the mouse; `MOUSE`, `STICK` or `KEYS` force one source and ignore the others (no handover, no warp on the forced source; the mouse stays warped only for (i)). A warp is Adapter-local presentation: it submits nothing, writes no block and reveals no sim state.
=====

Inputs owned here, consumed elsewhere.** `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` are two edge-triggered player inputs (pipeline C1) consumed by the pipeline's zoom ladder; `chart_table` calls `request_pause` (CR-15) through the menu in single-player and opens an overlay with the kernel `RUNNING` in co-op (CR-16); `inspect` enters the `inspect_card` context (the Adapter is the `INPUT_SURFACE` and owns the context; it publishes a presentation-local `{context, inspect_ref}` signal that In-World Instruments, a `PRESENTATION` surface, subscribe to — registry `inspect_card_context_signal`; never a command). content.content:
**D.10 Hold-to-confirm bar and tap-to-confirm**

The `confirm_bar` formula (Adapter-local, render time) is defined as:

`Δt_eff = 0 if kernel PAUSED else min(Δt, CONFIRM_DT_MAX_S);  b ← clamp(b + Δt_eff / CONFIRM_HOLD_S, 0, 1) while held;  b ← max(b − CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE × Δt_eff / CONFIRM_HOLD_S, 0) while released;  on b ≥ 1: submit the declared command once, b ← 0, require release before re-arm` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the bar added uncapped wall time per frame, so one 1 s hitch confirmed a destructive cut; re-review: the bar **freezes** under `PAUSED` (`Δt_eff = 0`; it neither fills nor drains), so a destructive hold can never complete during a pause and be rejected `PAUSED`, and on resume the hold continues only if the button is still down — the PC-2 resync submits the cancel otherwise)*

Derived (target latch): while `b > 0` the bar belongs to the focus `o_latched` captured when `b` left zero; a focus change does not move or complete it (it drains at 2× on `o_latched`, then the new focus starts from 0); completion submits for `o_latched` only
Derived (`give_up` surface) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the bar for `give_up` is drawn by HUD's DOWNED-only confirm plate (UI Requirements 1) from `confirm_view(seat)`; the plate exists for the whole time `loco_state == DOWNED` (published as `confirm_view.give_up_live`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and the bar arms only from a press edge observed while DOWNED (Edge Cases); the bar starts accumulating on the frame **after** the press edge, so with one rendered frame per tick the 0.8 s default fills 48 frames after the edge
Derived (per-verb hold; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D80 and D81; X10 is ruled) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: in the formula above read `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` as the verb's effective hold `H_v = min(m_v × confirm_hold_s, HOLD_EFF_MAX_S)`, where `confirm_hold_s` is the player's adjustable base hold (default `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` = 0.8 s), `m_v` is the multiplier the verb's owner declares (1 for every verb except the Chart Table's slot Delete, which declares 2, so Delete holds **1.6 s** at the default), and `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S` = 1.9 s is the ceiling that keeps invariant 7 true for every verb (derivation below). A player who cannot hold at all uses `confirm_mode = TAP` (two taps within `CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW`), which is selectable in Settings at MVP and not only in the one-handed preset
Derived (tap mode): tap 1 on focus `o` → `armed(o)` until `t_arm + CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW`, where `t_arm` and the window advance only while the kernel is not `PAUSED` (the timer is frozen under pause); tap 2 within the window on the same `o` → submit; focus change, context change or expiry → disarmed

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| Δt | float | render frame s | calculated (Presenter clock) | Frame delta — wall time; the sim never sees the bar |
| CONFIRM_HOLD_S (registry: `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`) | float | 0.6–1.9 (**0.8**) render s *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: was 0.6–1.2)* | data file; the player-adjustable Settings value `confirm_hold_s` starts here | Hold needed to confirm a destructive verb (base hold, before the verb multiplier) |
| m_v *(user rulings)* | int | {1, 2} (**1**; slot Delete **2**) | declared by the verb's owner (Interaction; Chart Table for Delete) | Per-verb multiple of the base hold |
| HOLD_EFF_MAX_S *(user rulings)* | float | 1.9 render s (derived) | calculated: `floor(10 × (max_age_ticks − 1) / TICK_RATE) / 10` = `floor(10 × 119 / 60) / 10` = 1.9 | Cap on any effective hold `H_v`; keeps `H_v × TICK_RATE = 114 < 120 = max_age_ticks(actions)` (invariant 7) at the largest base hold and the largest multiplier |
| CONFIRM_DT_MAX_S *(design review)* | float | 0.034–0.1 (**0.05**) render s *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: lower bound 1 / `MIN_TARGET_FPS` = 1/30, invariant 17)* | data file | Cap on the frame delta the bar may use; at 20 fps and above the bar is unaffected, a 1 s hitch adds 0.05 s (6 % of the hold) |
| CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE | float | 1.5–3 (**2.0**) | data file | Drain speed as a multiple of fill speed |
| b | float | 0–1 | calculated | Bar fill; drawn on the art bible 7.3 linear bar |
| CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW | float | 2–5 (**3**) render s | data file | Arm-to-confirm window in tap mode |
| confirm_mode | enum | {HOLD, TAP} (**HOLD**; one-handed preset **TAP**; selectable on its own at MVP) | Settings | The two-tap alternative to the hold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X10)* |

**Output Range:** `b` is clamped [0, 1]. Full drain from 1 takes `CONFIRM_HOLD_S / CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE` = 0.4 s; a release-and-re-press inside that window resumes from the drained value, so a nervous thumb is forgiven but a partial hold never completes by itself. Exactly one command per completion; the bar never auto-repeats while held (release is required to re-arm). The sim sees nothing until completion — one command, immediately pre-played — so **no window length can age a command**; the Section G invariant `H_v × TICK_RATE < max_age_ticks(actions)` (48 < 120 at the default; 96 for Delete at 1.6 s; 114 at the 1.9 s cap) is asserted only to keep a future two-command (arm/confirm) variant safe, and `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S` is what makes it hold for every base hold the player may set and every multiplier *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. At 60 fps the fill is 48 frames; at 30 fps, 24 frames of the same 0.8 s. A frame longer than 0.05 s (below 20 fps) fills only 0.05 s of the bar, so a hold at 10 fps takes longer than 0.8 s of wall time (honest: a hitching game does not confirm a destructive verb on one slow frame); a single 1 s frame advances `b` by 0.0625 and never submits.
**Example:** Hold for 0.5 s → `b = 0.625`; release 0.1 s → `b = 0.625 − 0.25 = 0.375`; re-press and hold 0.5 s → `b = 1.0` at 0.5 s → `cut_hatch {target}` submitted, bar resets, the pre-play starts. Per-verb hold *(user rulings)*: a slot Delete (`m_v = 2`) at the default base hold needs `H_v = min(2 × 0.8, 1.9) = 1.6 s` (96 ticks); with the player's base hold set to 1.2 s it needs `min(2.4, 1.9) = 1.9 s`, never more; a plain cut at 1.2 s needs 1.2 s. Tap mode: tap at `t = 10.0 s` arms the hatch; tap at `t = 12.9 s` confirms; a tap at `t = 13.1 s` would have found the arm expired and would re-arm instead.

7. `H_v × TICK_RATE < max_age_ticks(actions)` for every verb's effective hold `H_v = min(m_v × confirm_hold_s, HOLD_EFF_MAX_S)` — 48 < 120 at the default, 96 for Delete, 114 at the 1.9 s cap (D.10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X10, D80/D81; the player may now lengthen the base hold and Delete is 2×, so the check is on the effective hold; still one invariant; re-review: the count is now eighteen, the duplicate invariant 17 having been merged into I2.)*
